children.text: BREAKING · Council approves the harbour redevelopment plan after a nine-hour session

image.alt: The harbour at dusk, cranes idle over the redevelopment site

children.text: Harbour plan passes as council splits down the middle
Nine hours of testimony, one deciding vote and a promise that the fishing fleet keeps its berths. What the plan changes, and what it does not.
By Ines Okafor and Tomas Reyes · 14 minutes ago
Ferry crews vote to strike from Monday
Grain prices settle after a jittery week
Atlas 1.0 ships with a replayable machine
Lantern festival draws a record crowd
Opinion: the case for quieter streets

image.alt: A row of wind turbines on a ridge

children.text: The ridge lease attracted more interest than any since 2019, the ministry said.
The new library opens its doors
Twelve years after the fire, the reading rooms are back, with a roof garden on top.
Atlas 1.0 ships with a replayable machine
The simulator refuses to read a clock, and that turns out to be the whole product.
Ferry crews vote to strike from Monday
The union says the new roster leaves crews with nine-day stretches at sea; the operator says the roster is legal and the ferries will run.
Grain prices settle after a jittery week
Futures closed within a cent of Monday's open after a week that saw two of the biggest daily swings of the year.
Lantern festival draws a record crowd
Organisers counted forty thousand lanterns on the river, and a few in the trees.
Opinion: the case for quieter streets
Closing three streets to through traffic did not create gridlock. It created a place people wanted to stand around in.
